title: Man City's 115 charges, explained
checked: Status checked 3 Nov 2026: commission ruling published 29 Sep 2026 (all financial charges proven, most cooperation charges proven; widely reported as 114 of 115); City deny wrongdoing and lodged an appeal on 1 Oct 2026; no sanction set; appeal hearing expected around January 2027. Charge groups 54/14/5/7/35 (ESPN, LBC); £900m+ and Masters quote (NBC, Mishcon); 42-day hearing in 2024 (Mishcon); no CAS route, High Court possible (Sky); appeal by January (Al Jazeera). Sanctions listed as possible only.

lines.text: One hundred and fifteen charges. And this autumn, Manchester City finally got a verdict.
In twenty twenty-three, the Premier League charged City over nine seasons, two thousand nine to twenty eighteen.

scene.heading: FEBRUARY 2023
scene.body: The Premier League charges Manchester City with 115 breaches of its rules, covering 2009-10 to 2017-18, plus the investigation itself.

lines.text: Fifty-four on accounts. Fourteen on player and manager pay. Twelve on spending rules. Thirty-five for not cooperating.
The hearing ran forty-two days in twenty twenty-four. Then, nearly two years of silence.
On the twenty-ninth of September, the commission ruled.

scene.heading: 29 SEPTEMBER 2026
scene.body: Commission: every financial charge proven, plus most of the charges for failing to cooperate. Reports put it at 114 of 115.

lines.text: Every financial charge proven, plus most cooperation charges. Reports say one hundred and fourteen of one hundred and fifteen.
The finding: commercial deals that inflated City's income and cut its costs, by over nine hundred million pounds.
Premier League boss Richard Masters said the club systematically broke the rules for nearly a decade.

scene.text: The club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade.

lines.text: City say they are innocent, and they lodged an appeal on the first of October.
So right now, there is no punishment. That comes at a separate hearing, with no date set.
The appeal goes to three new independent judges, with a hearing expected around January.

scene.heading: WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
scene.body: Appeal Board of three, picked by the chair of the league's Judicial Panel. Hearing expected by January 2027. No Court of Arbitration for Sport this time.

lines.text: Possible punishments? Fines, a points deduction, even relegation or expulsion. None of it is decided.
So this series asks: what if City never had the money in question? Everything after this is imagined.
